chose: One bullet grammar: first line <name>: <sentence>, then indented key: value lines (protects, chokepoint, over, via, because, crossing, refuted, kinds, checklist)
because: a bullet stays readable as markdown, one invariant is one bullet as the glossary's spec concept requires, and indented key lines are the cheapest thing a scaffold can print and an agent can fill

chose: An invariant bullet may carry several enforcements, one per form: protects+chokepoint and over+via may both appear
over: exactly one enforcement form per bullet
because: the glossary's enforcement cardinality (reference decision d-6642c854) groups several enforcements under one invariant as evidence paths, and every Mnemion boundary claim names both a chokepoint and a test; forcing one form would drop a real witness

chose: A missing kinds line is a lack (the checklist was never run) and keeps the bullet a requirement; kinds: none records an examined empty set
over: absent kinds means no shape applies and the checklist is trivially satisfied
because: the checklist is the prosthetic for systematicity; if omitting kinds were the cheap path to invariant, the cheapest thing to produce would be the incomplete shape. Mirrors the journal's --over none rule: never examined and examined-empty are different facts

chose: A value still in <angle brackets> parses as a placeholder: the field counts as absent for state derivation and is listed as unfilled
because: scaffold output must parse so an agent can write it first and fill it second; an unfilled slot is a lack the check reports, not a broken spec

chose: Enforcement in a bullet reports as declared, unverified; refutation is present only when a refuted: line is recorded, for chokepoints too
over: treat a chokepoint form as self-refuted at parse time
because: the chokepoint's transparent refutation needs the language server (slice three); until it runs nothing has been witnessed, and the glossary says enforcement counts as detection only once its refutation is witnessed

chose: The retired section names and their replacements live in src/spec/retired-sections.json, a data file the vocabulary check does not read, and the retired-section test is generated from that table
over: string literals for the retired sections in the parser and tests
because: the parser must recognize the retired names to refuse them, and the vocabulary check would flag the literals in .ts and .md; a table of refused names is the same category of data as glossary.json, which the check also excludes

chose: Two checklist shapes are renamed in the seed: current-authority becomes revalidated-permission and legal-state-transitions becomes legal-state-succession; the kind tag for state changes is state, not transition
over: keep the seed names and tag list verbatim
because: authority and transition are rejected names, and a shape name is written into every spec that declares or dismisses it, so the seed would seed rejected names into every adopter

chose: Scaffold prints the bullet on stdout and the applicable shapes' sentences as guidance on stderr
because: the bullet must stay parseable and appendable, while the agent filling declare-or-dismiss lines needs each shape's sentence and applies-when in view

chose: The retired section names and their replacements live in src/spec/retired-sections.json, a data file the vocabulary check does not read, and the retired-section test is generated from that table
over: string literals for the retired sections in the parser and tests
because: the parser must recognize the retired names to refuse them, and the vocabulary check would flag the literals in .ts and .md files; a table of refused names is the same category of data as glossary.json, which the check also excludes

chose: A checklist shape may be declared as the bullet itself
over: declared-as must name a different invariant
because: the requirement often is the shape (kernel read+write capability is scoped-reads); refusing self-declaration would force a duplicate bullet or a dishonest dismissal

chose: Mnemion claims whose reference chokepoint symbol is itself the detector (findStoredDerivedAggregates, findUngatedCredentialMints) are rewritten in the totality oracle form only
over: keep the detector as the chokepoint symbol
because: a detector chokes nothing; naming it as the chokepoint would give the language server a symbol with no protected thing behind it, and the test it backs is the real enforcement

chose: The Features passes-test claim for pattern-effects totality is dropped; the Hive bullet at PATTERN_EFFECTS carries that test
because: one enforcement serves one invariant; a second bullet over the same test would be a second spelling with no invariant of its own

chose: Rationale in the retired why sections that named a real rule with no claim behind it (Auth register-token revalidation, Routing constant-time comparison and session revocation) is kept as requirement bullets rather than dropped
over: drop every why sentence without a claim
because: the reference prose called them candidates for promotion and recorded the bug each exists to kill; dropping them would lose the because while the rule still stands in code

observation: The storage kind makes nine checklist shapes apply to any storage requirement, and most were dismissed on Mnemion with one-line reasons
couldBe: the storage tag is too coarse and should split (at-rest, write path, fan-out)
nine is the right breadth and the dismissals are the point
discriminatedBy: after a few adopters, count dismissals per shape per kind; a shape dismissed nearly always under one kind with the same reason is mis-tagged

chose: The sixteen converted Mnemion claims carry no kinds line; only the bullets I authored (the seven system-doc rules plus the promoted candidates and the two refuted invariants) run the checklist
over: invent kinds and checklist answers for every converted claim
because: the checklist is the declaring agent's act of enumeration at the moment it holds the subject; filling it wholesale during a grammar conversion would record examinations that did not happen, and the check now reports each as lacking kinds so the debt is visible

chose: Mnemion's rewritten specs name identifiers as plain words, never in backticks
over: backticked identifiers as the reference wrote them
because: the vocabulary check nominates a backticked snake_case token seen twice as an unknown noun, and the kernel table names are not all glossary aliases; plain words keep the specs at zero unknown nouns without touching the domain glossary
